pairs.question: Numquidnam igitur fideles feminae sexum corporis amiserunt?
pairs.answer: Sed quia ibi renouantur ad imaginem dei ubi sexus nullus est, ibi factus est homo ad imaginem dei ubi sexus nullus est, hoc est in spiritu mentis suae.
pairs.derivation: Genuine interrogative (numquidnam expecting a negative) posed and answered by Augustine himself. Answer window is the contiguous sed-clause explaining why faithful women have not lost the image; window ends at the first full stop ('...spiritu mentis suae.'), before the next question 'Cur ergo uir...'. No framing to strip; first word and terminal punctuation already in source form.

pairs.question: Cur ergo uir propterea non debet caput uelare quia imago est et gloria dei, mulier autem debet quia gloria uiri est, quasi mulier non renouetur spiritu mentis suae, qui renouatur in agnitionem dei secundum imaginem eius qui creauit eum?
pairs.answer: Sed quia sexu corporis distat a uiro, rite potuit in eius corporali uelamento figurari pars illa rationis quae ad temporalia gubernanda deflectitur ut non maneat imago dei nisi ex qua parte mens hominis aeternis rationibus conspiciendis uel consulendis adhaerescit, quam non solum masculos sed etiam feminas habere manifestum est.
pairs.derivation: Real interrogative (cur ergo...?) answered by Augustine's own sed-clause giving the reason for the veiling figure. Answer window runs to the first full stop ('...habere manifestum est.'); the following sentence '[13] Ergo in eorum mentibus...' is stripped of its section marker and excluded as it begins a new conclusion. No framing words inside the quoted span.
